claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2. Docs: "A module consists of a collection of .tf, .tofu, .tf.json, and/or .tofu.json files that are kept together in a directory." "Every OpenTofu configuration has at least one module, known as its root module". "A module that has been called by another module is often referred to as a child module." Section 4 now reads "any folder of `.tf` files is one, and it becomes a child module when another configuration calls it", which matches.

Round 2. Module Sources: "A local path must begin with either `./` or `../` to indicate that a local path is intended". Module Blocks: "Most other arguments correspond to input variables defined by the module." Path: deploy/tofu/lessons/moved-into-module + ../../ = deploy/tofu, + modules/kind-cluster; the captured run (outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-moved.txt) plans and applies module.cluster from that folder.

Input Variables: "If present, the variable is considered to be optional and the default value will be used if no value is set" (default argument); "its value can be accessed from within expressions as `var.<NAME>`"; "When you declare them in child modules, the calling module should pass values in the `module` block." A variable is optional only when it has a default, so one without a default has to be given.

Output Values: "In a parent module, outputs of child modules are available in expressions as `module.<MODULE NAME>.<OUTPUT NAME>`." "The `value` argument takes an expression whose result is to be returned to the user."

Module Blocks: "The resources defined in a module are encapsulated, so the calling module cannot access their attributes directly." tofu validate: runs "checks that verify whether a configuration is syntactically valid and internally consistent", including "correctness of attribute names". tofu was not available to run here, so this rests on the docs alone.

Round 2: the claim now attributes the API-server meaning to the repo's own description. git show stage-3:deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster/outputs.tf: output "endpoint" with description = "Address of the cluster's API server, as seen from this machine." and value = kind_cluster.this.endpoint. The captured apply completes with all four attributes referenced, so they exist in tehcyx/kind 0.11.0.
git show stage-3:deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster/outputs.tf: output blocks endpoint, cluster_ca_certificate, client_certificate, client_key; only client_key has `sensitive = true`.

git show stage-3:deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster/variables.tf: variable "name" (type string, no default), "workers" (type number, default 0), "published_ports" (list(object), default []). main.tf line 16 writes node_image as a literal.

kind Quick Start: "Prebuilt images are hosted at kindest/node"; "Using a different image allows you to change the Kubernetes version of the created cluster." versions.yaml records kindest/node:v1.34.11@sha256:44e2... as kind v0.33.0's image for the 1.34 line. The module hardcodes that image (main.tf line 16 @stage-3), so every cluster it makes uses the same one.

Provider Requirements: "Each module must declare which providers it requires, so that OpenTofu can install and use them." "Provider requirements are declared in a `required_providers` block." kind-cluster/main.tf lines 5-12 @stage-3: source "tehcyx/kind", version "0.11.0".
main.tf @stage-3 lines 38-44: comment "One more node block per worker; with workers = 0 there is none." then dynamic "node" { for_each = range(var.workers) content { role = "worker" } }.

Version Constraints: version constraints are used by "The `required_version` setting" in the terraform block; "Both the root module and any child module can constrain the acceptable versions of OpenTofu"; `~>` "Allows only the rightmost version component to increment", so ~> 1.10.0 accepts 1.10.x only.

Resource Addressing: "A module path addresses a module within the tree of modules. It takes the form: module.module_name[module index]". Captured run at stage-3: `$ tofu state list` -> `module.cluster.kind_cluster.this`; plan lines show `module.cluster.kind_cluster.this will be created`.

outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-moved.txt (git show stage-3): "== without the moved block" / "  # kind_cluster.this will be destroyed" / "  # (because kind_cluster.this is not in configuration)" / "  # module.cluster.kind_cluster.this will be created" / "Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy." Refactoring docs: moving is understood "as an intent to destroy the object at the old address" and "to create a new object at the new address."

Refactoring: "OpenTofu treats an existing object at the old address as if it now belongs to the new address." The docs' own example is moved { from = aws_instance.a, to = module.x.aws_instance.a }. Captured run: "== with it" / "  # kind_cluster.this has moved to module.cluster.kind_cluster.this" / "Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy."
Captured run at stage-3: "Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed." then "$ tofu state list" / "module.cluster.kind_cluster.this".

tofu-moved.sh @stage-3 header line 3: "(after scripts/devops/tofu-state.sh). The state moves from lessons/first-cluster to lessons/moved-into-module." Lines 10-13 mv ../first-cluster/terraform.tfstate; lines 20-25 perl-strip the moved block, plan, restore; line 29 plan; line 31 `tofu apply -auto-approve -no-color`; line 33 `tofu state list`. Round 2: section 5's "applies with the `moved` block in place; the destroying plan is only shown, never applied" matches: the only apply runs after main.tf is restored.

kind: "kind is a tool for running local Kubernetes clusters using Docker container “nodes”." Destroying kind_cluster removes those node containers, and the recreated cluster starts from fresh nodes, so workloads that ran in the old cluster are gone.

This is an opinion, and section 6 gives it with its condition ("when callers truly need to differ in it, for example if one environment must try a new node image before another") and its cost. It is not stated as an unconditional rule.

kind Quick Start: "To see all the clusters you have created, you can use the `get clusters` command." Example: `kind get clusters` prints `kind` and `kind-2`. Captured run at stage-3: "Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed.", so donhang-iac is not deleted and stays listed. The kind get clusters output itself is not captured in the repo.

Output Values: "OpenTofu will hide values marked as sensitive in the messages from `tofu plan` and `tofu apply`." "OpenTofu will still record sensitive values in the state"; "anyone who can access the state data will have access to the sensitive values in cleartext."
